title: Strategy snapshot and decision slate for exec committee — roadmap spotlight
creator: Sofia Martinez
description: Assemble a concise, decision-focused packet (strategy snapshot + decision slate) for the upcoming exec committee meeting. Purpose: (1) align execs on tradeoffs across latency/cost/reliability investments tied to Growth OKRs, (2) request approval for two prioritized bets and a runway budget for a third, and (3) call out carryover risks that require leadership-level mitigation. Packet will include a one-page heatmap, three candidate investment proposals with expected impact and resource ask, and a recommended rollout cadence linked to Q2 milestones.
acceptance_criteria: One-page slide (PDF) summarizing current roadmap deltas vs. Growth OKRs and success metrics
Decision slate with 3 labeled asks (Approve / Defer / Reject) and associated cost/opportunity numbers
Stakeholder sign-off from Eng, Design, and Security on proposed scope and rough engineering estimates
Follow-up tracker created with owners and explicit next steps for approved asks
comments: 2026-02-06 — Sofia Martinez: Kickoff meeting notes: aligned with Eng and Design to keep packet <=6 slides. Initial heatmap draft attached under Links. Need clearer cost estimates for runtime kernel changes vs. Dedicated autoscaling enhancement.

2026-02-12 — Liam Chen: Eng estimate for 'Autoscaling policy revamp' = 3 sprint teams for 6 weeks. Risk: may overlap with dedicated capacity backlog. Suggested we present as 'Phase 1: low-risk policy changes' to reduce scope.
2026-02-16 — Priya Rao (Design): Shared two visual options for the heatmap: simplified quadrant vs. stacked-bar. Recommend quadrant for execs for faster signal recognition. Updated visuals linked.

2026-02-20 — Marcus Yeo (Engineering Lead): Kernel-selection experiment data: 12% median token latency improvement for targeted models but requires extra QA for quantized model variants. Proposed gating condition: roll out to batch workloads first.

2026-02-24 — Sofia Martinez: Incorporated Marcus notes and added a mitigation path recommending a canary window + automatic rollback. Added line item for observability instrumentation (estimated +$10k infra spend).
2026-02-27 — Security (Aisha Patel): Reviewed decision slate; no PII exposure risk but request to add KMS key rotation timeline for Private deployments tied to approved investments.

2026-02-28 — Liam Chen: Packet ready for pre-read. Requested exec decision on prioritization between 'Autoscaling policy revamp' and 'Kernel scheduling optimizations' — both are P1 asks with different risk profiles.
decisions: Request 1: Approve 'Autoscaling policy revamp' (target: reduce 95th percentile latency spikes on hosted endpoints) — ask: 3 squads, 6 weeks, $120k runway. Expected benefit: 18% fewer SLA incidents for PLG customers.

Request 2: Approve 'Focused kernel scheduling & quantization pilot' (target: 10–15% token-cost reduction on high-throughput models) — ask: 1 squad, experimental budget $60k, run as canary for 8 weeks.

Request 3: Defer 'Dedicated capacity UX overhaul' to next cycle unless additional headcount approved — current scope would require re-prioritizing Dedicated backlog and delaying Dedicated SLA improvements.

Recommended exec action: approve Requests 1 and 2 with conditional go/no-go checkpoints (end of sprint 2 and canary completion), and allocate a contingency fund of $25k for unexpected infra instrumentation needs.
risks: Engineering capacity risk: concurrent Dedicated roadmap work may create resource contention for Autoscaling revamp
Quality/regression risk: kernel scheduling changes could surface accuracy regressions on quantized models; requires expanded eval set and QA time
Customer-impact risk: if Autoscaling revamp is delayed, we expect a transient uptick in timeout incidents for mid-tier PLG customers during peak traffic
Budget risk: runway estimates assume no major cloud egress increase; if experiments trigger higher-than-expected token churn, we may need additional spend
